_comment_include: No Next-generated type artifacts here (`next-env.d.ts`, `.next/types/**`,
`.next/dev/types/**`). The ROOT stopped being a Next app when `src/app/`
and `next.config.ts` were deleted 2026-08-08; the surviving Next app is
`viewer/`, which this tsconfig EXCLUDES and which carries its own.
Those entries were not merely dead — `next-env.d.ts` carries
`/// <reference types="next" />`, which loads Next's global augmentation
of `NodeJS.ProcessEnv` (`readonly NODE_ENV: 'development'|'production'|
'test'`) into every file in the repo. MEASURED 2026-08-13: that made a
required, read-only NODE_ENV apply to code that has nothing to do with
Next, producing 36 errors across three unrelated subsystems — 25 TS2345
(a test's fake env object 'missing' NODE_ENV), 6 TS2540 and 5 TS2704
(cannot assign to / delete a read-only NODE_ENV). Deleting the stale
generated `next-env.d.ts` took it to 0.
The file is gitignored, so a fresh clone never had the problem and only
machines that once ran a root Next build did.
The guard is the `next-env.d.ts` entry in `exclude` below, NOT its absence
from `include`. Dropping it from `include` alone is cosmetic and was
MEASURED to be: `**/*.ts` matches `next-env.d.ts` on its own, so with the
file recreated the same 36 errors returned. Only `exclude` outranks the
glob.
